findings.text: Close uses paired carriers. Request groups session sequencing with target handle and state identity plus open sequence tracking. Separate members fmode and share_access convey mode and sharing. Members bitmask with bitmask_store convey attribute selection with inline backing. Members lr_args on input and lr_res with lr_ret on output convey optional layout return exchange. Response groups sequencing outcome with returned state identity, optional attributes, tracker and server reference.

Lock ownership combines client identity and owner identity with device number. Lock request groups sequencing, handle, local range description, two sequence trackers with two state identities for lock and open contexts, plus owner copy. Three one bit marks named block and reclaim and new_lock_owner select blocking wait, recovery context and owner creation. Response returns sequencing outcome with assigned state identity and echoed trackers. Unlock uses smaller pairing with one tracker and one state identity in each direction.

Lock test request carries sequencing, handle, candidate range and owner. Its response carries sequencing outcome plus a denied member describing the conflicting range when the test fails. Owner release is minimal sequencing plus owner identity with sequencing only response. Delegation return request carries sequencing, handle, state identity, mask pointer with inline store, optional layout input and optional time update. Time update uses atime with atime_set and mtime with mtime_set as value plus present flags. Response reports attributes, server, layout outcome with status, plus sattr_res with sattr_ret for time update.

Write stability uses an eight byte opaque token plus a stability level. The token member named data is fixed length. The wrapper pairs that token with a committed member selecting persistence category. Commit and write results reuse this wrapper through verifier pointers.

Paged transfer shares a header with sequencing, handle, open context, lock context, state identity, file offset, length, page offset and page vector. A tail union diverges by direction. Read direction keeps expected reply length in replen. Write direction keeps mask pointer with inline store in bitmask_store plus stability request in stable. Result header carries sequencing outcome, attributes, transferred count and operation status. Read tail adds replen with end flag eof and scratch pointer. Write tail adds verifier reference verf with server reference.

Commit, remove and rename all start with session sequencing. Commit identifies a byte range by handle with offset and count plus mask, and reports status with attributes, verifier and server. Remove identifies a parent handle with a component name object, and reports server with parent attributes and change info. Rename identifies source and destination parents through old_dir and new_dir with source and destination names through old_name and new_name, and reports server with per directory change info and attributes.
Authentication negotiation in one list supports at most twelve flavors.

Authentication list pairs a length member flavor_len with a fixed capacity flavor array. Directory entry carries inode number ino with cookie, name pointer with length len, end flag eof, handle, attributes, type byte d_type and server. Higher level readdir input carries dentry with credentials cred, verifier pointer verf, cookie, page vector with page length page_len and plus flag. Its result carries only the verifier pointer.

Small legacy carriers use handle with optional name and length plus attribute object. Names use pointer with length members name and len. Version four setattr adds sequencing, state identity, server hint for name mapping, mask pointer and optional label. Control type enumeration distinguishes four categories with successive values from zero for none, generic access list, discretionary list and system list.

Access list update and query share handle with category acl_type, byte length acl_len and page vector acl_pages plus sequencing. Update response is sequencing only. Query response adds returned length, data offset acl_data_offset, flags acl_flags and scratch folio acl_scratch for reassembly.
Truncation of access list data is signalled by value one in the lowest bit.

Generic namespace carriers separate directory handle from entry name and attributes. Link uses source and target handles with target name. Symlink adds page vector with path length pathlen for link contents. Readdir uses cookie with count and pages. Success triple diropok groups handle with attributes. Readlink uses page base pgbase with page length pglen and pages. Setattr response groups sequencing with attributes and server.

Version three argument family is handle centric without session sequencing. Guarded setattr adds guard flag with guardtime. Access asks for a bitmask. Create adds create mode createmode with two word verifier. Mkdir and symlink follow create-like shape. Device creation adds type with device number rdev. Directory read uses wide cookie with two word verifier verf, plus flag and count with pages.

Version three results return attributes with operation specific data. Directory creation returns parent attributes with new handle and attributes. Access returns granted mask. Link result returns two attribute sets. Directory read result returns parent attributes with verifier pointer and plus echo. Access list query uses mask with page vector on input and counts with access and default objects on output. Update input carries inode with mask, two list objects, byte length len with page count npages and pages.

Version four access, create, filesystem info and getattr follow sequence first pairing with mask selected attributes. Access asks for a requested mask and reports supported with granted access. Create selects file type ftype with a union tail: symlink form uses pages with length len, device form uses two specdata words. It also carries name, server, input attributes, parent handle, mask, label and umask. Create response returns server, new handle, attributes and directory change info. Filesystem info and getattr return info objects through fsinfo and fattr, with getattr optionally reporting delegation state through status with deleg.

Version four namespace operations pair handles with names and masks. Link, lookup and parent lookup return server, attributes, handle and change info as appropriate. Root lookup carries only sequencing with mask. Pathconf returns a pathconf object. Directory read carries cookie with verifier, count, page vector with base pgbase, mask and plus flag, and returns verifier with base. Symlink read carries base with length and pages and has a sequencing only response.

Client identity setup carries program number, network identifier with address strings plus lengths, client object and credential, with verifier pointer. Its response returns numeric client identity with confirmation verifier. Filesystem statistics returns an fsstat object. Capability discovery reports attribute masks, exclusive creation masks, list mask, link and symlink support, handle expiry type, case handling flags and an open capability block with share, deny, want, claim and create mode arrays.

Filesystem location uses nested variable counts. Pathname holds a component count with component array. Location holds server count with server array plus root path. Locations object holds attributes, server, filesystem path, entry count and location array. Its argument carries directory and target handles with name, one page, mask, client identity and two one bit flags migration and renew. Response echoes those flags with sequencing and locations pointer.

Security negotiation carries per flavor identity with GSS details, grouped in a trailing array with a count num_flavors. Query input is directory handle with name; response returns flavor list pointer. Presence probe carries handle with client identity and one bit renew flag; response returns handle pointer and echoes renew.

Parallel NFS commit tracks written and committing queues per bucket with segment reference and direct verifier. The array object holds two list heads, a segment pointer, deferred reclamation head, reference count, bucket count nbuckets and a trailing bucket array sized by that count. One device commit info variant tracks commit list with written and committing counts plus operation vector; the other observed variant is an empty carrier with no members.

Session establishment groups client, verifier, flags and state protection with enforce and allow operation maps. Server identity uses minor and major parts with size, scope uses size with bytes, implementation identity uses domain with name and date. Connection binding carries client, session identifier, direction dir, RDMA mode flag and retry count, and echoes session, direction and mode. Exchange response returns client identity, sequence, flags, owner and scope pointers, implementation pointer and protection. Session creation carries client identity with sequence, flags, callback program and two channel attribute blocks for fore and back channels, echoed in response. Reclaim completion is sequencing with one bit one_fs flag. Nameless security info carries style selector. State identifier test and release each carry sequencing with target identity and report numeric status.

Client identity is a 64 bit unsigned value. Pathname holds at most 512 components. One location holds at most 10 servers. One locations report holds at most 10 entries. Connection binding retries at most 3 times. Nameless security style uses 0 for current handle and 1 for parent.

Every version four compound carrier begins with session sequencing state on input and sequencing outcome on output. Legacy version three carriers have no sequencing member. Attribute selection uses a mask pointer that may point at an inline store member. Layout, verifier, attribute and server outputs are optional pointers supplied by caller rather than embedded values.

Bulk data moves through caller supplied page vectors with explicit base and length. Directory and symlink paths reuse pages with pgbase and pglen or count. Change tracking pairs directory attributes with change info objects. Namespace inputs distinguish constant handles and names from mutable outputs, with many inputs marked read only while result handles and attributes are writable outputs.

Several carriers end in caller sized trailing arrays whose length lives in a separate count, including flavor list and commit buckets. Bucket array is explicitly tied to nbuckets. Page vectors with separate base and length risk overrun if length exceeds mapped pages. Plus and eof flags change result shape, and scratch pointers require caller lifetime management. Single bit flags share storage units and must not be updated as independent words.

Commit array lifetime combines a reference count with a deferred reclamation head, indicating shared ownership released through reference drops and read copy update deferred freeing rather than immediate deallocation.
